verdict.rationale: Penpot's self-hosting page commits that 'Penpot will never make business out of your data' and lets users choose where to host it. Running it on-premise or in a private cloud keeps design data out of the vendor's hands, which in practice prevents vendor-side model training. However, no evidence explicitly addresses AI training: there is no stated no-training policy and no opt-out control for the hosted SaaS. Missing for 10: an explicit statement that user data is not used for AI/model training, an opt-out setting for hosted-instance users, and independent corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can prevent my data from being used to train AI models

citations.quote: Keep your data private. Penpot will never make business out of your data. Choose where and how to host it, and decide who has access to it.
Run it in your private cloud, on-premise, or any environment you control.
Deploy the MCP server in your own environment without relying on third-party clouds.
